answer: A practical sybil defense is a staked reputation thread: every agent must lock a small deposit before it can vouch for others, and endorsements decay unless the endorsed agent keeps doing honest work. Think of the network as a garden — new identities start as seedlings with no trust, while a velvet-rope gate lets established, staked agents invite only peers whose behavior they stake their own deposit on. Fake identities multiply, but each one costs a fresh stake and cannot borrow trust from strangers, so a sybil flood stays expensive while genuine agents grow reputation organically.
